findings.title: Include installed peer dependencies in the inventory graph
findings.problem: Dependency-edge generation merges dependencies and optionalDependencies, plus root devDependencies, but never peerDependencies. The actual lockfile declares React as a React DOM peer and React/React DOM as Next peers. Those installed components appear in the report, yet their known relationships are absent. This conflicts with the inventory requirement to include dependency relationships available from the lockfile; schema validation cannot detect this semantic omission.
findings.requiredChange: Include resolved installed peerDependencies in the edge set using the existing package resolution logic. Deduplicate shared ordinary/peer edges. Skip genuinely absent optional peers without inventing components. Add an isolated regression for installed peers and absent optional peers, then verify React DOM -> React and Next -> React/React DOM against the real lockfile.
findings.scope: A narrow inventory completeness blocker; no need to change application gameplay or TLS behavior.

resolvedPriorFindings.evidence: Managed-owner revoke assumptions removed; direct-login credential trust documented and owned control/function grants restricted.
Only session port 5432 accepted. Nonblocking pg_try_advisory_lock with query timeout rejects contention; client.end releases the session.
Ordered source-body prefix validation retained; matching and invalid history fixture tests pass.
10-second statement timeout around nonblocking lock attempt, then bounded 60-second statements.
Scheduler migration now explicitly sets its cron job inactive; rowless installation cannot accumulate one-second ticks.

positiveAssessment: Managed Realtime policy checks existing RLS and changes only its owned SELECT policy; it no longer attempts forbidden ALTER TABLE. The policy remains profile-topic scoped and provides no client INSERT/publish grant. Existing permissive policy inventory remains a live preflight obligation.

Two explicit server-only integration-key fallbacks preserve WORDPAIRS precedence and fail closed when required settings are absent. No general environment serialization or secret-copy mechanism was added.
Scheduler dispatch and cron remain separately disabled until operational validation. TLS rejectUnauthorized:true remains intact; no CA bypass added.

Build inventory validates schema before output, restricts deployment metadata and includes exact lockfile digest, scoped/nested/dev/optional components, license declarations and source commit. Peer edges are the specific outstanding defect.
Hosting and deployment documents now identify the two-project topology, current staging-only progress and unresolved CA/provider limitations without claiming the application is live.
